result:
The world contains so many layers—some visible, some hidden, like the quiet hum of a city at 3 a.m. or the way a single photograph can hold an entire universe of unspoken emotions. I often think about how we’re all just temporary collections of stardust, briefly organized into beings capable of love, suffering, and curiosity. What does a tree feel when its roots touch the memories of another tree planted a century ago? Do the shadows we cast whisper stories to the walls we pass?

And then there’s the absurdity of it all: the way we take ourselves so seriously, yet laugh at a dog chasing its tail, unaware that we, too, circle our own repetitive thoughts. Maybe the point isn’t to find answers but to keep asking better questions. Or maybe it’s simpler—to let the wind carry the things we can’t name, and to be kind while we’re here.

What’s on your mind? I’d love to hear.
